paragraphs: On Saturday evening, Lily read an email from Grace, her pen pal in Singapore. "Ms. Ong read us this story in class," Grace wrote. Lily told the story to Tom in the living room. Pip lay on Tom's feet and listened.

Long ago, a mouse, a rabbit, and a bear lived near a green hill. In the hill, there was a secret cave. Nobody went in, because it was dark. One day, the three friends decided to explore it. The mouse did not say much, but she looked at everything. The bear laughed at her, because she was so small. "Come on!" said the bear. "I am big, and I am not afraid."

Inside the cave, there was such a big room with shiny stones. The friends looked at the stones for a long time. Then a big stone fell and closed the exit. The cave was very dark now. They could not see their own hands. The bear pushed the stone, but it did not move. The rabbit pushed too, and it did not move. "We are in trouble," said the rabbit. "We cannot get out."

"Wait," said the mouse. "I can see a small light under the stone." "There is a hole." The mouse was small, so she went into the hole and dug with her feet. Soon the hole was bigger, and the rabbit dug too. Then the bear pushed the stone, and it moved. The friends ran out into the bright sun. "Thank you, little mouse," said the bear. "In the future, I will never laugh at small friends." The mouse smiled.

Tom looked at Lily when the story finished. "The mouse was small, but she was important," he said. "What is the theme?" asked Lily. "Every friend is important," said Tom. "They saved themselves together." Pip heard the word "mouse" and looked under the sofa. He looked for Squeaky, but there was no mouse there. Lily laughed and gave him a little hug.
text.summary: Lily tells Tom a story from her pen pal Grace. A mouse, a rabbit, and a bear explore a secret cave, and the small mouse finds the way out, so the theme is that every friend is important.
